posts.title: A day at the red pot
posts.excerpt: How a pale skein becomes kankurenai red in one slow afternoon.
posts.content:
We soak the skeins overnight, then lower them into the pot of madder and safflower when the water is just too hot for a finger.

Two hours later we lift them out, rinse them in the yard and hang them on the bamboo pole. The red always looks darker wet; it settles by morning.

posts.title: Why we knit a swatch first
posts.excerpt: Ten minutes and a small square save a sweater that fits nobody.
posts.content:
Every hand knits a little tighter or looser than the pattern. Cast on twenty-four stitches, knit a square, wash it and let it dry flat.

Bring it to the table and we count the stitches together, then choose the needle size that makes your sweater the size you wanted.

posts.title: A scarf before the snow
posts.excerpt: Two skeins of chunky wool and three weekends: our favourite first project.
posts.content:
A plain scarf in garter stitch teaches everything a beginner needs: casting on, an even tension and how to join a new skein.

Start in October and it is ready when the first snow reaches the lane. Hang it by the window and it keeps its colour for years.
